metadata.title: Worker max_interval Within Observed Cycle Reality

rules.statement: Every active worker's configured `schedule.max_interval` in .intent/workers/<stem>.yaml MUST accommodate the worker's observed cycle reality. The audit aggregates `worker.heartbeat` rows from core.blackboard_entries over a PER-WORKER evidence window of max(24h, (10 + 1) x the worker's declared max_interval), uncapped, computes the p95 gap between consecutive heartbeats per worker_uuid, and fires a finding when observed p95 exceeds configured max_interval x 1.1. Compliance for this rule requires real evidence: a worker with fewer than 10 heartbeat samples in its window, or whose evaluation could not run at all (e.g. no DB session available), is UNAVAILABLE -- not silently compliant. A worker whose required window exceeds the configured worker.heartbeat retention (blackboard.telemetry_ttl_days, if the subject is under a telemetry prefix) is an UNSATISFIABLE configuration, reported as such -- never as a worker failure and never as insufficient samples. An unavailable dependency/evidence source for this blocking rule forces the audit verdict to DEGRADED, never PASS and never FAIL (see .intent/enforcement/config/audit_verdict.yaml, any_blocking_unavailable_rules). The finding for a genuine drift includes the configured value, the observed p95, and the bump target so the operator can update the YAML in one read.
rules.rationale: ADR-041 implemented per-worker liveness thresholds via schedule.max_interval, but never validated that configured values match observed cycle reality. As workloads grew, configured-vs-observed drift accumulated silently and surfaced as worker.silent false-positive findings -- 9,125 in a 7-day window (62% of all abandons) at the time #516 was filed. The 600s default doesn't fit any of the 10 active workers it's assigned to: average gaps already exceed the threshold. Manual bumps (today's commit 329919d4) don't solve the recurrence problem: values will drift out of fit again as work grows. This rule is the missing invariant ADR-041 should have enforced. The 1.1 multiplier accommodates measurement jitter without papering over drift; the 10-sample minimum prevents alarms during daemon-restart warm-up windows. Configured-vs-observed gap audit runs at reporting until each currently-unfit worker has had its YAML bumped; promotion to blocking follows the ADR-091 D2 ramp once a clean cycle confirms zero violations. ADR-103 pins `schedule.max_interval` as a cycle cap (the contract this rule enforces) and pins the 1.1 multiplier as jitter tolerance, not as a tolerance budget operators may spend -- a finding here means real cycle has grown past the cap, not that the rule is too tight. WORDING CORRECTION (#856): the statement previously said insufficient-evidence workers are 'skipped silently'; that was a true description of a G9 defect (URS-production-readiness.md: 'crashes degrade, never comply'), not an intended contract. _check_worker_max_interval_within_observed now surfaces both a missing db_session and per-worker insufficient-sample evidence as one aggregated ENFORCEMENT_UNAVAILABLE finding each (GitHub annotation-budget preserved), which the audit-verdict policy routes to DEGRADED for this blocking rule. WINDOW CORRECTION (governor ruling 2026-09-17, exposed by the #895 cold review as a generic runtime-rule defect, not a Trial 0 exception): the original fixed 24h window could never hold 10 gaps for a worker whose declared max_interval exceeds ~2.4h (llm_partition_archiver 86400s -> 1 sample; llm_partition_maintainer and var_tmp_janitor 21600s -> 3 each), so the rule reported UNKNOWN for those workers indefinitely -- a structurally impossible control, which certification cannot knowingly accept. The window is now per worker, max(24h, 11 x max_interval); the extra interval keeps boundary timing from making the tenth gap unattainable, and there is deliberately no cap because a cap shorter than the required window recreates the defect. Retention is verified against the governed operational config rather than assumed. Grouping stays by declared worker_uuid, not process instance: a restart appears as one large gap inside the window rather than resetting the evidence, which is the honest reading of a cycle cap. For a daily worker ten gaps genuinely need about eleven days of uninterrupted evidence.
